12:27 Coy is trying too hard to defend it. Great storytelling is great storytelling no matter the medium. Was it underwhelming? Definitely. It didn’t have to be an apocalypse level kind of thing, but simple writing, do the things you say your story and your characters are going to do, if you can’t and choose to go in another direction, all it would take is one or a few lines to address it. For me, this show has been doing a rinse and repeat since S2, just so they could get to their season 5. If your story cannot justify or answer questions on the actions taken by your characters, then obviously you have failed. If the decisions made by your characters are not within character, do not make sense for the story being told in the moment and only serve to set up a future narrative, then you have failed. There are much better shows out there that were told without the need of big battle scenes and it made sense for the story. And if you are saying, it was all in service of the characters, not necessarily the narrative, then I point you to shows that are much better character pieces than whatever that finale was trying to be: The Penguin, Peacemaker S1&2
